headline: Prediction Round Activity - Curiosity Builder for ESL Lessons
outcomes: Students commit to predictions before seeing the answer, which makes the reveal more memorable
The activity builds useful language for guessing, probability, evidence, and changing your mind
Teachers create a purpose for reading, listening, or watching because students want to check their predictions
The class starts with curiosity instead of passive input
howItWorks: LessonCaptain generates three prediction prompts related to the lesson topic or source
Students choose or write predictions from their own device before the reveal
The teacher shows the class distribution and invites students to explain their reasoning
After the source, reading, or discussion, the class returns to the predictions and checks what changed
teacherUseCases: Before a YouTube or listening lesson, ask students to predict what will happen or what the speaker will say
Before a reading, build interest around the main claim, conflict, or outcome
Before a culture or travel lesson, surface assumptions the class can test during the lesson

faq.q: What language does Prediction Round practise?
faq.a: Students practise prediction phrases, probability language, giving reasons, and revising an opinion after new information. It is useful before almost any source-based lesson.

faq.q: Does the prediction have to be correct?
faq.a: No. The value is in committing to a guess and explaining the reasoning. Wrong predictions often create better discussion because students can explain what evidence changed their mind.

faq.q: Can I use this with a video lesson?
faq.a: Yes. Prediction Round is a natural opener before a video because students watch with a purpose: to confirm, reject, or adjust their own prediction.

faq.q: Does it work with beginner students?
faq.a: Yes. Beginners can choose from short options, while stronger students can write their own predictions and justify them with more complex language.

faq.q: How do students lock in their predictions?
faq.a: No. Students answer from a browser link and do not need to install anything or sign in.
